name: Modal
summary: A modal is a dialog over a dimmed page that has to be dealt with before anything else. Use the native <dialog> element opened with showModal(), which supplies the top layer, the backdrop, inertness and the focus trap. What it leaves you is where focus lands when it opens, and that is the decision people get wrong.
demoNote: Open example 1 and Tab past the last button: focus comes back around, because the browser does that for a dialog opened with showModal(). Open example 3 and press Enter without looking — the answer under it keeps the project.

contract.useWhen: A native dialog over the page. showModal() traps focus; you decide where it lands.
keyboard: cycles inside — showModal() makes the rest of the page inert
activates the focused button, which is why the safe one is under it
closes through the cancel event, so unsaved work can intercept it
failureModes: aria-modal=true added by hand, which has made VoiceOver skip the dialog's own content
showModal() with no scroll lock — and overflow:hidden alone jumps the layout sideways
aria-expanded on the trigger, reporting on a thing the person is now inside
the outcome announced from a region inside the dialog, removed from the tree before it speaks
no visible close control, which is a trap on touch
a drag that starts inside and ends on the backdrop, closing the dialog
api: AC.createModal(root, options) -> { open, close, isOpen, triggers, element, destroy }
